title: Week-by-week sprint buffer budget & hiring scrub
summary: Working sheet to map 12-week sprint-level buffer funding, skeleton hiring plan and dynamic pricing triggers to smooth token-cost shocks and preserve runway.
body:
Purpose:
This is a working spreadsheet-style memo for the finance and product partnership to: 1) define a week-by-week buffer for sprint-level capacity shocks, 2) produce a minimal hiring skeleton (roles, timing, cost phasing) that can be toggled on/off, and 3) attach pricing-sensitivity trigger rules that inform temporary slab adjustments or burst credits. Not final — experimental assumptions and gating logic are intentionally conservative.

High-level approach:
- Time horizon: 12 weeks (quarter sprint view) with week-level granularity for burst readiness.
- Buffer funding: a reserved pool (operational buffer) sized in GPU-hours and token-credit dollars to absorb 15–35% spike events for mid-tail customers.
- Hiring skeleton: minimal hires by sprint to support steady state + two surge scenarios. Hires are staged as contractor-first then FTE conversion if sustained demand.
- Pricing triggers: two-tiered triggers (soft and hard) based on rolling 7-day token burn and margin delta. Soft -> temporary add-on credits; Hard -> temporary slab price increase + HC gating.

Assumptions (base case):
- Base token burn (hosted API) = 350M tokens/week across platform.
- Average token unit cost to Redwood = $0.00018/token (weighted model mix).
- Average realized price per token = $0.00048/token.
- Latency-tiered SLA reserve: plan 3% of capacity for latency SLO failover.
- Hiring cost assumptions: contractor GPU-engineer fully loaded = $135k/year equivalent; FTE SWE infra fully loaded = $230k/year equivalent.

Week-by-week buffer table (illustrative):
Week | Expected tokens (M) | Buffer tokens (M) | Buffer $ | Notes
W1   | 350                 | 80                | $14,400 | initial buffer funded from ops reserves
W2   | 360                 | 70                | $12,600 | demand climb; monitor model mix shift
W3   | 410                 | 130               | $23,400 | mid-quarter event; soft trigger active
W4   | 330                 | 50                | $9,000  | normalizing
...  | ...                 | ...               | ...     | ...
W12  | 375                 | 90                | $16,200 | end of quarter runway check

Buffer sizing rationale:
- Buffer tokens sized by 90th–95th percentile of weekly spikes in historical traffic windows similar accounts.
- Convert tokens -> $ using weighted unit cost; keep $ buffer as quick-settlement credits to customers or to buy short-term cloud/GPU spot capacity.

Hiring skeleton (toggleable):
- Sprint 0 (weeks 1–2): no new FTEs. Prioritize contractors: 1x contractor GPU infra engineer (4 weeks), 1x temp SRE (4 weeks). Estimated incremental cost: $27k.
- Sprint 1–3 (weeks 3–8): add 1x SWE infra (contractor -> convert to FTE if >6 weeks sustained), 0.5x product manager (fractional), ramp professional services for enterprise onboarding. Estimated incremental run-rate if converted: +$18k/week equivalent.
- Sprint 4 (weeks 9–12): convert 50% of contractors to FTE only if sustained delta in capacity >20% for 6 consecutive weeks.

Contingent scenarios (two):
- Scenario A (short spike): single-week 80% token surge in top-10 customers. Response: draw buffer tokens, enable soft trigger credits (-10% to affected customers for next 2 weeks), increase spot-GPU budget for week. No hires.
- Scenario B (prolonged uplift): sustained +30% baseline for 6+ weeks. Response: accelerate contractor conversions, open 2 FTE reqs (infra SWE, SRE), and initiate price slab rebalancing for new consumption delta.

Pricing sensitivity triggers (operational rules):
- Soft trigger (warning): rolling 7-day burn > baseline * 1.2 AND margin delta < -6% -> finance approves up to $X of credits or spot budget shift; ops evaluates cache/batching knob changes.
- Hard trigger (escalation): rolling 7-day burn > baseline * 1.35 OR burst > baseline * 1.8 in a single day -> immediate price slab uplift (temporary 5–12% increase for new usage), initiate hiring gating call, and notify sales/CS for customer communication.

Decision gates and governance:
- Weekly finance ops sync (Fri) reviews buffer drawdown and recommends either replenish (move budget) or reduce next sprint buffer by 10–20%.
- Hiring triggers require: (a) 2 consecutive weeks in Scenario B OR (b) product/solutions backlog growth metric > 15% tied to performance incidents.
- Customer communications: PS + CSM drafts templates for soft credit vs hard price change. Legal must pre-approve words for SLA and credits.

Quick sensitivity sketch (price vs headcount):
- If realized price falls by 10% with flat demand -> runway shortens by ~6–8 weeks given current burn unless we: 1) reduce buffer allocations, 2) delay conversions, 3) accelerate slab price changes for new users.
- If token unit cost increases by 15% (GPU spot price spike) -> recommended immediate 10% buffer top-up for next 2 sprints while procurement locks longer-term spot inventory.

Open questions / items to finalize:
- Exact dollar cap for soft-trigger credits (proposal: $75k/week across platform).
- Approval matrix for converting contractors mid-sprint (who signs off: finance + eng manager + People Ops).
- Which price slabs can be temporarily elevated without impacting active contracts. Legal to advise.
- Region-specific buffer sizing (APAC vs NA) — need regional token telemetry breakouts.

Next steps (owner/action):
- Maya: finalize week-level telemetry pulls to validate 90/95 percentile buffer numbers (due 2026-02-19).
- Ethan: prototype an automated trigger dashboard in Looker and a weekly alert (due 2026-02-26).
- Priya: draft customer credit/cs messaging templates and legal-ready wording (due 2026-03-05).
- Oliver: simulate 3 pricing-sensitivity Monte Carlo runs (base, price-compression, GPU-spot-spike) and attach expected runway deltas (due 2026-03-03).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc is intentionally conservative on conversions; contractors are the lever of choice for quick scale.
- Keep the buffer fungible between token credits and short-term capacity purchase to avoid lock-in.
- Expect iterations — this is a sprintable playbook to be improved after the Looker prototype shows actual trigger frequency.

Attachment checklist (for final version):
- Week-level token telemetry CSV (12 weeks)
- Contractor vs FTE cost model (spreadsheet)
- Legal template for temporary slab adjustments
- Suggested customer-facing email templates for credits and for price adjustments
